philosophers_stone.name: Philosopher's Stone
philosophers_stone.lore: The alchemists called their goal the Great Work and wrote that it passes through three colors: the blackening, the whitening, and at last the reddening, when the Stone appears. Zosimos of Panopolis sought it in Roman Egypt. Copyists claimed that Nicolas Flamel made it in Paris. The Emerald Tablet, ascribed to Hermes Trismegistus, puts the method in one line: that which is above is like that which is below. None of them held this. It is red, heavier than gold, and warm as a living hand. What it is carried past, it shows truly. Abaddon kept it in the Pit because its last change needs sunlight.

bronze_bull.name: Bronze Bull Idol
bronze_bull.lore: Minos prayed to Poseidon for a sign that Crete was his to rule, and the god sent a white bull walking out of the surf, to be given back in sacrifice. Minos thought it too fine to kill and offered a lesser animal. Poseidon's punishment fell on the king's house: the Minotaur, Asterion, was born of it, and the Labyrinth was built to hide him. This small bronze bull has been worn smooth by centuries of hands. It still smells faintly of sea-foam, and it still wants to be given back at sacred water.

eye_of_graeae.name: Eye of the Graeae
eye_of_graeae.lore: A single milky eye, cold as a sea-stone. The three Grey Sisters, Deino, Enyo and Pemphredo, were born old, and they had one eye and one tooth among them, passed from hand to hand. Perseus waited until the eye was between two sisters and all three were blind, and took it. He would not give it back until they told him the road to Medusa. It goes on watching from inside a pack. The gods rewarded that piece of cunning at a place sacred to Athena, and they might again.

cats_footstep.name: Sound of a Cat's Footstep
cats_footstep.lore: A glass vial that makes no sound when shaken. The gods had twice bound the wolf Fenrir with iron, and twice he had burst the chain. So Odin sent to the dwarves, who asked for six things. This was the first: the noise a cat makes when it walks. Snorri adds, quite seriously, that this is why a cat's step has made no sound from that day on. The dwarves used all there was.

womans_beard.name: Roots of a Woman's Beard
womans_beard.lore: A twist of fine filaments, like hair, that the eye keeps sliding off. It is the second of the six things the dwarves of Svartalfheim worked into the fetter Gleipnir: the beard of a woman. The old storyteller who wrote the recipe down told his listener to check it against the world. Women have no beards, he pointed out, because the dwarves took them all.

mountain_root.name: Root of a Mountain
mountain_root.lore: A gnarled tendril of grey stone, cool and very slightly flexible. A mountain looks as though it ought to be rooted like a tree, but dig beneath one and there is only more stone. The Norse account explains why: the dwarves pulled up every root there was for the binding of the wolf Fenrir. This piece was left on the workshop floor.

fish_breath.name: Breath of a Fish
fish_breath.lore: A sealed bubble that smells of deep water and cold currents. Fish do not breathe air, and no one has ever seen the breath of one hang in a winter morning. According to the Norse reckoning there used to be such a thing, until the dwarves gathered all of it for the cord that holds the wolf. The bubble turns slowly, as if still looking for the surface.

bird_spittle.name: Spittle of a Bird
bird_spittle.lore: One bright drop that keeps its shape and glistens without any light to help it. It is the last ingredient of Gleipnir: the spittle of a bird. Fenrir himself now drools enough to fill a river, which the Norse call Van, where he lies bound with a sword propping his jaws. The birds gave up theirs so that he could be put there.

bear_sinew.name: Sinew of a Bear's Sensitivity
bear_sinew.lore: A pale thread, something between nerve and tendon, that twitches now and then as if it had felt something move. The dwarves asked for the sinews of a bear, the cords that carry feeling through that enormous body, and wove them into the wolf's fetter with five other things that no longer exist. It senses what its bearer cannot.

gleipnir.name: Gleipnir
gleipnir.lore: The first chain the gods made for Fenrir was called Leyding, and the second, twice as strong, Dromi. He snapped both. The third is this: a ribbon as smooth and soft as silk, made by the dwarves from six things that are not in the world any more. The wolf smelled a trick and would not be bound unless a god laid a hand between his jaws as a pledge. Only Tyr stepped forward. The ribbon tightened the more the wolf struggled, and all the gods laughed except Tyr, who lost his hand. It has never been broken.

leather_scrap.name: leather scrap
leather_scrap.lore: A stiff offcut of leather, the corner a cobbler trims away at the toe or heel of a shoe. It is too small to patch armor and too hard to bind a wound. There is an old custom in the north that such trimmings should never be saved or reused, only thrown aside. Someone is said to be collecting them, and to be in no hurry.

seal_of_wrath.name: Seal of Wrath
seal_of_wrath.lore: A blood-red disc, hot as a coin left in the fire, with the smell of brimstone on it. John of Patmos saw a scroll in heaven sealed with seven seals, and woe followed the breaking of each. The Pit has seven of its own, and this was kept by the first of its guardians. It came away from the demon's body only when the demon was dead.

seal_of_pestilence.name: Seal of Pestilence
seal_of_pestilence.lore: A sickly green disc that weeps something foul and makes the air around it hum like a cloud of flies. Tradition gives the rider on the white horse a crown, a bow and the name of Pestilence, and sends him out conquering. The demon that carried this seal did the same work in the dark below. It holds the Pit shut a little less well for every hand it passes through.

seal_of_famine.name: Seal of Famine
seal_of_famine.lore: A withered disc the color of dead grain. The third rider of the Apocalypse sits a black horse and holds a pair of scales, and a voice names his prices: a day's wage for a measure of wheat. Whoever holds this seal feels that arithmetic in the stomach, as though days had passed since the last meal. It is one of the seven locks on the Abyss.

seal_of_war.name: Seal of War
seal_of_war.lore: A rust-red disc etched with crossed blades. To the rider on the red horse was given a great sword, and power to take peace from the earth so that men should kill one another. The seal trembles with the memory of it: the shouting, the standards, the ground afterward. A demon wore it as a badge of office, and the Pit was the office.

seal_of_death.name: Seal of Death
seal_of_death.lore: A pale disc, cold as a headstone in January. John wrote: behold a pale horse, and his name that sat on him was Death, and Hell followed with him. The shadow of whoever holds this seal grows darker and a little longer than it should be. The demon that carried it is dead. The seal does not seem to have noticed.

seal_of_earthquake.name: Seal of the Earthquake
seal_of_earthquake.lore: A cracked grey disc that shivers in the hand. When the sixth seal was opened, John saw a great earthquake: the sun turned black as sackcloth, the moon became as blood, and every mountain and island was moved out of its place. The stone underfoot groans when this is carried over it, as if it remembered the order and expected it again.

seal_of_silence.name: Seal of Silence
seal_of_silence.lore: A disc of pale silver that swallows sound; near it even breathing is muffled. When the Lamb opened the seventh seal there was silence in heaven for about half an hour, and then the seven trumpets were handed out. This is the last lock on the Pit and the worst, because of what the quiet is waiting for.

scales_of_michael.name: Scales of Michael
scales_of_michael.lore: Michael's name is a question, 'Who is like God?', and it was his battle cry when he threw the Dragon out of heaven. Painters show him with a sword in one hand and a pair of scales in the other, weighing souls at the Judgment while a devil tries to tip the pan. These are the scales. In the Book of Revelation the king of the locusts of the Abyss is named Abaddon, the Destroyer. When he opens the Pit, the Host answers these scales: for every locust that rises, an angel comes down.

cursed_lodestone.name: Cursed Lodestone
cursed_lodestone.lore: Thales of Miletus said the lodestone must have a soul, because it moves iron without touching it. This one has a will as well. It is a massive black stone that drinks the light around it, and it weighs as much as a small anvil. A dying knight begged a stranger to carry it for the sake of his wife, and the curse binds it to anyone who takes it up freely. It cannot be set down. Only a scroll of Remove Curse will break the bond, and the promise would still be owed.

sealed_dispatch.name: Sealed Dispatch
sealed_dispatch.lore: An iron-bound scroll case closed with the wax seal of the City Watch. Inside are the positions of the companies defending a city under siege, and thousands of lives ride on its reaching the surface. The courier who carried it this far could go no farther and asked with his last breath that someone else finish the run. It is heavy and of no use underground. It is a promise, which is a different kind of weight.

palladium.name: Palladium
palladium.lore: A wooden image of armed Athena, small enough to carry under one arm. The Trojans said it fell from heaven at the feet of their founder Ilus, and a prophecy held that Troy could not fall while it stayed inside the walls. So Odysseus and Diomedes crept in by night and stole it, and only then was the Horse worth building. The goddess of sound strategy still favors whoever carries her likeness: the way down shows itself to the bearer through stone and darkness alike.

tablet_of_destinies.name: Tablet of Destinies
tablet_of_destinies.lore: The Tablet of Destinies made its holder master of what must be. Enlil, chief of the gods of Sumer, wore it at his breast and set it aside only to bathe. The lion-headed storm-bird Anzu, who guarded his door, watched for that moment, seized the Tablet and flew to the mountains, and every decree of heaven fell silent. Ninurta hunted him down with arrows and brought it back. It lets its bearer refuse one verdict in each place: a wrong answer is unsaid, the clay cracks a little further, and a different question is asked.

vidars_sandal.name: Vidar's Sandal
vidars_sandal.lore: Vidar, the silent son of Odin, owns a shoe that has been in the making since the world began. It is pieced together from the scraps cobblers trim from the toes and heels of every shoe, which is why the Norse say a man who wants to help the gods should throw those scraps away. At Ragnarok the wolf Fenrir will swallow Odin. Then Vidar will plant this shoe on the wolf's lower jaw, take the upper jaw in his hand, and tear him apart.
vidars_sandal._design_note: MEGA-SECRET quest reward. AC is modest (1 + leather material bonus) — the value is the instant-kill on Fenrir, not the defensive line. peak_weight 0.0 ensures it never natural-spawns; the altar assembly path is the only way in. Code references: src/game_combat.py:1292-1311 (instant-kill trigger), src/game_divine.py:499-521 (altar assembly), src/dungeon.py:2145-2154 (altar carve). See tools/balance/systems/bosses_and_quests.md §Fenrir Quest Layer 2.

pandoras_box.name: Pandora's Box

chaos_table.desc: Plague released -- you and all enemies in sight are poisoned for 30 turns.
Toil released -- enemies in sight gain +1 attack chain capacity; you lose 1 for 50 turns.
Strife released -- a random monster in sight turns hostile to all others (and you).
Famine released -- hunger meter drops 25%.
Madness released -- a random stat drops by 1 for 100 turns.
Lies released -- one unidentified item gains a false flavor description for 100 turns.
Old Age released -- DEX -2 for 50 turns.
Despair released -- lose 5 SP and cannot SP-cast for 20 turns.
Tempest released -- a lightning bolt strikes a random tile in sight (4d6).
Polymorph one -- a random hostile in sight becomes a mouse for 30 turns.
Foresight kept -- you gain Clairvoyant for 50 turns.
Toil-mastery -- +1 chain capacity on all quizzes for 50 turns.
Memory of Eden -- +1 to a random stat for 50 turns.
Friendship -- the nearest hostile monster is charmed for 30 turns.
Curiosity rewarded -- all unidentified items in inventory are identified.
Beauty unleashed -- monsters within 2 tiles cannot attack you for 5 turns.
Health restored -- HP and SP refilled to full.
Foreknowledge -- full mini-map for current floor revealed.
Strength of will -- 3 turns of Protected and 50 turns of Hasted.
Hope -- permanent +1 to a random stat.

chaos_table_failure_skew.description: On quiz failure, re-roll a 1d20 with the lower half mapped to negative effects (rolls 1-14 = rolls 1-14 of chaos_table) and rolls 15-20 mapped to chaos_table rolls 11-16. The 'Hope' roll (20) is unavailable on failure -- you cannot grasp Hope by sloppy theology.

pandoras_box.lore: Hesiod, who told the story first, calls it a pithos: a clay storage jar as tall as a man. More than two thousand years later the scholar Erasmus mistranslated the word, and it has been a box ever since. Zeus sent Pandora and her jar to Epimetheus, whose brother Prometheus had warned him to accept no gifts from Olympus. She lifted the lid. Sickness, toil and every sorrow flew out over the earth, and she clapped it shut with only Hope left inside, caught under the rim. This one is small, sealed with wax and cord, and painted with fleeing figures.

aladdins_lamp.name: Aladdin's Lamp

item.desc: Wish for an item. The player names a category (weapon / armor / shield / accessory / artifact / wand / scroll / spellbook / potion). The djinn generates a random item of that category at ONE TIER ABOVE the current floor's normal loot tier. For 'artifact', the djinn produces a random non-quest artifact not currently in the player's inventory.

power.desc: Wish for a power. Choose ONE: permanent +1 to any single stat (player picks STR/CON/DEX/INT/WIS/PER, no cap override), OR a permanent status immunity (player picks from the immunity list).

entity.desc: Wish for a named entity. Choose ONE: summon a powerful ally for 50 turns (paladin, archmage, or holy warrior -- equivalent to a tier-5 charmed monster), OR reveal the location, name, and weakness of the next boss/unique-monster on a future floor.

wish_fallback_effects.desc: A random item from a randomly chosen category appears, but at ONE TIER BELOW the current floor's normal loot tier.
Permanent +1 to a RANDOM stat (not player's choice).
100 turns of a random temporary status immunity (poison, paralysis, fear, sleep, blindness, or confusion).
Summon a random tier-3 ally for 25 turns (half normal duration).
Reveal only the next boss's floor location -- no name, no weakness.

aladdins_lamp.lore: A brass oil lamp, dented and tarnished, worth nothing at market. The tale of Aladdin was not in the old Arabic manuscripts of the Thousand and One Nights. A Syrian storyteller named Hanna Diyab told it to the Frenchman Antoine Galland in Paris in 1709, and Galland wrote it in. A sorcerer from the far west sends a tailor's idle son into a cave for a lamp he calls worthless. The jinni bound in this one is patient and exact. It grants a single wish to a worthy hand, and half of one to an unworthy hand.

soul_sphere.name: Soul Sphere
soul_sphere.lore: A sphere of crimson and ivory that hums with trapped souls. Ancient texts say these vessels were used to bind creature spirits. One wonders what might happen if it were hurled with force...

unusual_soul_sphere.name: Unusual Soul Sphere
unusual_soul_sphere.lore: An unusual soul sphere. Its colors are black and silver. It pulses with a powerful energy...

lions_thorn.name: Lion's Thorn
lions_thorn.lore: A black thorn as long as a finger, drawn from the paw of a lion who took it better than expected. Aulus Gellius tells of a runaway slave named Androcles who did a lion the same service in an African cave. Years later the two met again on the sand of the Circus, in front of all Rome, and the lion remembered. A lion's memory is long, and this still smells of him.

cuthberts_gospel.name: Saint Cuthbert's Gospel
cuthberts_gospel.lore: A Gospel of John small enough for a pocket, bound in red leather worked with a vine. It lay in the coffin of Cuthbert of Lindisfarne, the shepherd who became a bishop and would rather have stayed a hermit. When the longships came, the monks lifted coffin and book together and carried them from place to place for seven years. The last bearer sent it down to a chapel where his brothers wait. It is worth a great deal of money to the wrong people, and it was handed over on a promise.
